notes:
I couldn't do this research. My first attempt to fetch the source pages failed with an error saying I had no tool calls left for this turn, and a second try failed the same way. So I haven't read a single page.

Your rules say to report only what the pages actually say and to give a URL for every point. That means I can't honestly write any notes yet. Anything I wrote about Psalm 70 now would come from memory, not from the sites, so I've left it all out.

In a new turn, I planned to read these pages first:

- **Traditional verse-by-verse reading:** Enduring Word on Psalm 70 (enduringword.com/bible-commentary/psalm-70/); Gill, Ellicott and the Pulpit Commentary on Bible Hub (biblehub.com/commentaries/[gill|ellicott|pulpit]/psalms/70.htm); and Precept Austin's Psalm 70 page.
- **Other Protestant traditions:** searches on spurgeon.org (*Treasury of David*), wesley.nnu.edu (Wesley's notes), desiringgod.org, ligonier.org, lcms.org / 1517.org and the Pentecostal sites. These would show whether the traditions actually differ on any verse. Psalm 70 may turn out to have few real disputes.
- **Other views:**
  - NET Bible notes, for v. 1's "To bring remembrance" and Psalm 70 nearly repeating Psalm 40:13–17.
  - Bible Odyssey.
  - New Advent, which has Augustine on this psalm under the older numbering (Psalm 69). It also has John Cassian's *Conferences* 10, which builds a prayer method on v. 1 that's well known in Catholic and Orthodox practice. I'd check that against the actual page before including it.
  - Searches for any prosperity or word-of-faith use of the psalm, included only if the sites discuss it.

If you send the request again, I'll start with these sources and write the notes verse by verse with a URL for each point.
